module.html_intel.checks: Collects from the home page the generator, comments, e-mail addresses, forms (action, password), internal IP addresses, server paths, hidden fields and technical error messages.
module.html_intel.fix:
If the page contains a password, token, API key or identifier (comment, hidden field, script), revoke it and create a new one before cleaning up the page: removing it from the HTML does not invalidate it, and it may have been copied, cached or archived.
Form sent in clear text: serve the whole site over HTTPS (valid certificate, `301` redirect from HTTP to HTTPS, HSTS), then make every `action` attribute point to an `https://` address or a relative path (HTML and nginx snippets). If passwords may have travelled in clear text, force their reset.
Technical error message displayed (PHP, SQL, Java, .NET, Python): turn off error display in production (`display_errors = Off`, `DEBUG = False`, custom error pages), record the details in the server logs and fix the cause of the error.
Internal IP addresses and server paths visible in the code: remove them from templates, comments, attributes and scripts. Also check that this internal service cannot be reached from the Internet.
Sensitive HTML comments (passwords, to-do notes, internal paths): remove development comments from pages served in production. Use the template engine's own comments, which are not sent to the browser, rather than HTML comments, or strip comments at build time or with a minification tool.
`generator` tag announcing the version: remove the tag or at least its version number (setting of the CMS, the theme or a security plugin), and update the software.
Check: `curl -s https://example.com/ | grep -nE '<!--|action="http:|generator'` must no longer show a sensitive comment, a form pointing to `http:` or a version. Then run the scan again.
module.html_intel.title: HTML intelligence
module.html_intel.why: HTML code often betrays the infrastructure: a displayed PHP error, an internal IP in a comment or a login form in clear text help an attacker and expose visitors.
